workflow step numbers & \texttt{fragment 134-139, ligate 152-154, index 156-157} & ``The library then undergoes fragmentation and adapter ligation (Part 2, Steps 134-139 and 152-154). ... Illumina P5 and P7 sequence adapters and a final sub-library index are also appended at this final PCR step (Part 2, Step 157). e, A 0.5-0.7x double size selection then selects out unwanted fragments'' \citep{gaisserHighthroughputSinglecellTranscriptomics2024}\,\texttt{(md:82)} {\color{tcgray}\emph{Note:} This is the correction. One precision caveat: the quote names step 157 for the index PCR, and 156 comes from the numbered protocol body rather than from this sentence.} \\
\addlinespace[2.5pt]
Cas9 route, guide pool and conditions & \texttt{253 sgRNAs} & ``We designed 253 sgRNA spacer sequences to target the 5S, 16S, and 23S rRNA sequences in E. coli and P. putida, weighted proportionally to the regions in the rRNA that appeared more frequently during NGS after microSPLiT. ... 100 pmoles of the transcribed, column-purified sgRNA molecules were pre-incubated with 10 pmoles spCas9 (NEB) ... then incubated at 37 C for 2 hours.'' \citep{brandnerPooledSinglecellCRISPRa2025}\,\texttt{(md:151)} \\
\addlinespace[2.5pt]
Cas9 route, measured outcome & \texttt{4.6\% -\textgreater{} 60.2\%; 2.2\% -\textgreater{} 10.4\%} & ``With rRNA depletion, the mRNA fraction increased from 4.6\% to 60.2\% (Fig. 2B) and median mRNA transcripts per cell more than doubled, from 54 to 115 [E. coli]; ... the mRNA fraction increased from 2.2\% to 10.4\% [P. putida, md:119]'' \citep{brandnerPooledSinglecellCRISPRa2025}\,\texttt{(md:71)} {\color{tcgray}\emph{Note:} Two organisms, one protocol, and the gap between them is the transfer risk the figure is drawing attention to. Both figures are proportions of ALIGNED transcripts computed before single-cell filtering, not of reads purchased.} \\
\addlinespace[2.5pt]
RNase H chosen over Cas9 & \texttt{75-80\% rRNA left by the Cas9 arm} & ``after testing two approaches for depleting ribosomal sequences from bulk libraries (Extended Data Fig. 3a-c), we chose an RNase H-based approach to complete our pipeline [and, md:92:] this is consistent with our trial runs using Cas9-based rRNA depletion (75-80\% rRNA in the final library, Extended Data Fig. 3a)'' \citep{wangSinglecellMassivelyparallelMultiplexed2023}\,\texttt{(md:23)} {\color{tcgray}\emph{Note:} The head-to-head. An earlier version of Sec. 3.5 cited M3-seq as corroborating the Cas9 route; it tested both and chose the other one.} \\
\addlinespace[2.5pt]
in-situ route, best published result & \texttt{\textasciitilde{}2.5-fold, \textasciitilde{}7\% of total RNA} & ``we then tested polyadenylation with E. coli poly(A) polymerase I (PAP) ...; 5'-phosphate-dependent exonuclease ("Terminator", Epicentre); and RT with ribosomal RNA-specific probes followed by RNaseH mediated degradation ... \addlinespace[2.5pt]
why M3-seq avoids in-situ depletion & \texttt{in situ can decrease mRNA capture} & ``we noted that depletion of rRNA in situ can decrease mRNA capture efficiency and thus focused on depleting rRNAs after amplification'' \citep{wangSinglecellMassivelyparallelMultiplexed2023}\,\texttt{(md:23)} \\
\addlinespace[2.5pt]
undepleted yeast transcript proportions & \texttt{93.7\% rRNA, 5.75\% mRNA} & ``On average, the transcript proportions we recover are 93.7\% rRNA, 0.005\% tRNA, 0.04\% ncRNA, and 5.75\% mRNA.'' \citep{brettnerUltraHighthroughputMassively2024}\,\texttt{(md:70)} {\color{tcgray}\emph{Note:} Computed with multi-mapping reads RETAINED (STARsolo, 'the most basic uniform multi-mapping algorithm', md:195), which is the convention that inflates apparent rRNA. \addlinespace[2.5pt]
